stem.text: Two parts of a sailing boat are the mast and the boom. The mast is a vertical rigid beam and the boom is a horizontal rigid beam. One end of the boom is attached to the mast by a pivot. The other end of the boom is connected to the mast by a rope, as shown.

stem.alt: Diagram of a vertical mast and a horizontal boom attached to it at a pivot. A rope runs from the top of the mast to the far end of the boom, labelled rope, with tension T and an angle of 40 degrees marked to the horizontal. A downward arrow labelled 200 N acts on the boom.

stem.text: The rope is at an angle of $40^{\circ}$ to the horizontal and exerts a tension force $T$ on the boom. The weight of the boom is $200\,\text{N}$. The mass of the boom is uniformly distributed along its length. The boom is in equilibrium.
